exposure: concomitant gastrointestinal tract anomalies/disorders (ischemic bowel/necrotizing enterocolitis, intestinal malrotation, duodenal web, hiatal hernia, gastroschisis)
cohort: The study included 13 neonates diagnosed with gastric perforation, identified from medical charts reviewed from January 1997 through December 2008.
finding: Neonatal gastric perforation is often concomitant with GI anomalies or inflammatory/infectious disease, and patients who were outborn, had leukopenia on admission, peritonitis, and thrombocytopenia development within 48 hours were at risk for poor outcome.
